pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR5 Pasir Ris station (EWL interchange). Serves central Pasir Ris town, connecting CRL to the East-West Line. Opens as part of 12-station Phase 1 bloc.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR5. EWL interchange. Phase 1 tunnelling stretches complete as of 2026; first CR151 trainset delivered to Singapore May 31 2026. LTA target 2030, no delay signal.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR4 Pasir Ris East station. Serves eastern Pasir Ris residential area along Pasir Ris Drive 1, between Pasir Ris Street 11 and 12.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR4. Non-interchange. Officially named Pasir Ris East. Provides a second CRL stop within Pasir Ris town.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Punggol Extension — CP1/CR5 Pasir Ris junction station. Acts as the branch node connecting CRL main line to the Punggol Extension spur toward Punggol.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CP1 (same physical station as CR5). EWL + CRL multi-interchange. Construction design underway per LTA March 2026 factsheet. 7.3 km extension, progressing smoothly.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR6 Tampines North station. Integrated Transport Hub with Tampines North Bus Interchange. Serves Tampines North HDB estates and Elias Road/Terrace residential clusters.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR6. Non-interchange. Primarily serves Tampines North sub-estate. Tampines East residents benefit via bus feeder to ITH. Tampines West and central Tampines already served by existing DTL/EWL.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR8 Hougang station (NEL interchange). Connects Cross Island Line with the North-East Line at existing Hougang NEL station.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR8. NEL interchange (NE14). Sengkang residents gain a new cross-island route option via NEL transfer at Hougang. Tunnelling work on this section reported complete.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR7 Defu station. Serves the Defu industrial and Hougang residential fringe, providing access from Hougang town's western reaches.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR7. Non-interchange. Located in Hougang planning area near Defu industrial estate. Working name is 'Defu'; pending formal naming.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR9 Serangoon North station. Serves Serangoon North HDB estate and nearby schools including Rosyth School and Bowen Secondary.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR9. Non-interchange. First MRT access for Serangoon North estate which has historically relied on bus services. Working name 'Serangoon North'.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR10 Tavistock station. Serves Tavistock / central Ang Mo Kio fringe area, connecting the AMK corridor between Serangoon North and Ang Mo Kio interchange.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR10. Non-interchange. Located in the Ang Mo Kio planning area near Tavistock Avenue. Addresses long under-served corridor between AMK and Serangoon North.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR11 Ang Mo Kio station (NSL interchange). Connects Cross Island Line with the North-South Line at Ang Mo Kio, integrating with AMK Hub and Bus Interchange.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR11. NSL interchange (NS16). Gives AMK residents direct cross-island connectivity east toward Tampines/Pasir Ris and west toward Clementi/Jurong without changing at Bishan or city.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR12 Teck Ghee station. Serves the Teck Ghee HDB estate in Ang Mo Kio planning area, filling a gap between AMK and Bright Hill stations.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR12. Non-interchange. Located in Teck Ghee sub-estate of Ang Mo Kio; working name 'Teck Ghee'. Bishan fringe residents near Sin Ming also benefit.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Phase 1 — CR13 Bright Hill station (TEL interchange). Western terminus of Phase 1, connecting to the Thomson-East Coast Line at Bright Hill, serving the Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park corridor.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CR13. TEL interchange (TE7). Located in Bishan planning area. Provides Bishan residents a new cross-island axis and dramatically improves east-west connectivity from Bishan without going through the city centre.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Punggol Extension — CP2 Elias station. New station serving the Elias Road corridor in Pasir Ris / Punggol borderland, providing first rail access to that area.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CP2. Non-interchange. Located between Pasir Ris and Punggol towns. Working name 'Elias'. Construction design underway as of LTA March 2026 update.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Punggol Extension — CP3 Riviera station (Punggol LRT East Loop interchange). Connects CRL spur to the Punggol LRT network at Riviera station.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CP3. Punggol LRT interchange (PE4). Gives Punggol LRT users a direct CRL connection. Over 40,000 households in Punggol benefit from the extension.

pipeline_items.description: CRL Punggol Extension — CP4 Punggol station (NEL + Punggol LRT interchange). Terminal of the Punggol Extension, co-located with existing NEL Punggol station and Punggol LRT hub.
pipeline_items.notes: Station code CP4. Triple interchange: NEL (NE17), Punggol LRT (PTC). Travel time between Punggol and Pasir Ris cut to 15 minutes. 70,000 daily journeys shortened per LTA. Construction design and build underway, progressing smoothly per LTA March 2026 factsheet.

pipeline_items.description: JRL Stage 1 (JRL West): 10 stations from Choa Chu Kang (JS1) to Boon Lay (JS8), Gek Poh (JW1), and Tawas (JW2). Originally planned for end-2027, officially delayed by 6 months to mid-2028. Confirmed by Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow at MOT Committee of Supply Debate on 4 March 2026. Reasons: PIE viaduct construction restricted to overnight closures, canal viaduct required deeper ground reinforcement, COVID-19 recovery shortfall. Interim shuttle buses operational from end-2027. Choa Chu Kang station (JS1/NS4/BP1) is triple interchange with NSL and Bukit Panjang LRT — Bukit Panjang benefits via this interchange.
pipeline_items.notes: Mid-2028 is the LTA-confirmed revised date as of March 2026. The original end-2027 target has formally slipped by 6 months — this is a gazetted delay, not a rumour. Bukit Panjang benefits indirectly: JS1 at Choa Chu Kang is a triple interchange (NS4/JS1/BP1) with the Bukit Panjang LRT. No further slippage announced as of June 2026 but construction still ongoing. Stage 1 stations in order: JS1 Choa Chu Kang, JS2 Choa Chu Kang West, JS3 Tengah, JS4 Hong Kah, JS5 Corporation, JS6 Jurong West, JS7 Bahar Junction, JS8 Boon Lay, JW1 Gek Poh, JW2 Tawas.

pipeline_items.description: JRL Stage 2 (JRL East): 7 stations from Tengah Plantation (JE1) to Pandan Reservoir (JE7). Key interchange at Jurong East (JE5/NS1/EW24). Serves the eastern fringe of Tengah new town (Tengah Plantation, Tengah Park), Bukit Batok West (JE3), Toh Guan, and Jurong East. Stage 2 date has not been formally revised since March 2026 — carries the original planned year of 2028.
pipeline_items.notes: 2028 is the LTA-published planned year on the official JRL project page, but it has NOT been formally re-confirmed post the March 2026 slip announcement (which only addressed Stage 1). Treat as gazetted/planned. Stage 2 stations: JE1 Tengah Plantation, JE2 Tengah Park, JE3 Bukit Batok West, JE4 Toh Guan, JE5 Jurong East, JE6 Jurong Town Hall, JE7 Pandan Reservoir. Apply rail slip premium (0.85) per framework invariants — 2028 may become 2029 given Stage 1 already slipped.

pipeline_items.description: JRL Stage 3 (JRL West Extension): 7 stations extending south toward Jurong Pier and west to NTU. Stations: JS9 Enterprise, JS10 Tukang, JS11 Jurong Hill, JS12 Jurong Pier, JW3 Nanyang Gateway, JW4 Nanyang Crescent, JW5 Peng Kang Hill. Serves NTU Nanyang campus and Jurong industrial/waterfront corridor.
pipeline_items.notes: 2029 is the LTA-published planned year on the official JRL project page. Not formally re-confirmed post-March 2026. Jurong East benefits marginally as it already has JE5 interchange in Stage 2 — Stage 3 expands the line south and west. Primary beneficiary is Jurong waterfront/industrial zone and NTU, not a residential estate in scope. Apply rail slip premium — 2029 could become 2030. Estates: Jurong East (extended catchment via Tukang/Enterprise), NTU area.

pipeline_items.description: JRL JS2A infill station: New station announced 4 March 2026 at MOT COS Debate. Located between JS2 (Choa Chu Kang West) and JS3 (Tengah). Will serve the Forest Hill district of Tengah new town. Built as a shell structure initially — trains will pass through the shell for first several years before fit-out commences. Brings total JRL stations to 25.
pipeline_items.notes: LTA confirmed the station will be built but targeted to open in mid-2030s, timed to match completion of Forest Hill district developments in Tengah. Civil works for the shell structure commenced as of the March 2026 announcement. Will not open with Stage 1 in mid-2028 — trains pass through without stopping. Expected year set to 2035 as midpoint of mid-2030s; actual year is TBC pending Tengah development pace.

pipeline_items.description: CCL6: Circle Line Stage 6 — Keppel, Cantonment, Prince Edward Road stations open, completing the full Circle loop (HarbourFront–Marina Bay closure). Confirmed passenger service 12 July 2026; public preview 4 July 2026.
pipeline_items.notes: LTA confirmed. Keppel (CC29) and Cantonment (CC30) serve Bukit Merah / Tanjong Pagar fringe. Prince Edward Road (CC31) sits at the Queenstown/Central edge. Completes the Circle Line — no more dead-end at HarbourFront or Dhoby Ghaut. Queenstown already provisioned B+; incremental gain is marginal given existing CCL and MRT density. Bukit Merah (currently rail-thin) gains more meaningfully.

pipeline_items.description: TEL Stage 5: Bedok South (TE30) and Sungei Bedok (TE31) open, extending the Thomson-East Coast Line from Bayshore. Sungei Bedok is a DTL interchange. Target: 2H 2026 — no specific date confirmed as of June 2026.
pipeline_items.notes: LTA announced 2H 2026 in December 2024. Exact date not yet set; TEL service adjustments running May–July 2026 suggest imminent final testing. Bedok South serves the Bayshore/East Coast Park precinct — primarily a new-supply area (Bayshore BTO) rather than existing estate resale uplift. Sungei Bedok DTL interchange expands east-west connectivity. Bedok town gains a second TEL touchpoint after Bedok (EWL) and Upper East Coast. Use 2026 but flag as not confirmed-dated.

pipeline_items.description: JB–Singapore RTS Link: Woodlands North (Singapore) to Bukit Chagar (JB) standalone LRT across the Straits of Johor. ~5-minute cross-border journey. Connects underground to TEL Woodlands North station.
pipeline_items.notes: Targeted December 2026; first train demo at Woodlands North completed February 2026. Parliament Cross-Border Railways Bill (May 2026) references end-2026 target. Some risk of slip to early 2027 during final systems testing — apply rail SlipPremium (0.85) in discount. This is a standalone LRT, not an MRT extension; pipeline entry captures the connectivity uplift to Woodlands Causeway corridor. Woodlands already carries a Causeway-discount in Value scores; RTS reduces that discount structurally.

pipeline_items.description: Founders' Memorial MRT station (TE22A) on the TEL opens alongside the Founders' Memorial museum. Station is physically built but trains currently skip it.
pipeline_items.notes: Station already constructed between Gardens by the Bay and Tanjong Rhu TEL stations. Opening tied to Founders' Memorial completion, itself contingent on museum fit-out. No residential estate meaningfully uplift — Bay East Garden / Marina Bay fringe is commercial/tourism. Include for completeness; negligible impact on residential Provision scores.

pipeline_items.description: Jurong Region Line (JRL) Stage 1: 24 stations on the main trunk from Choa Chu Kang to Boon Lay and the first western branch section (Bahar Junction to Tawas). Interchanges at Choa Chu Kang (NSL/BPLRT) and Boon Lay (EWL). Delayed from 2027 to mid-2028.
pipeline_items.notes: LTA confirmed delay to mid-2028 in March 2026 (originally late 2027). Key stations include Corporation, Gek Poh, Bahar Junction. Serves existing HDB stock in western Jurong; Choa Chu Kang West specifically adds a new stop within CCK. Jurong West gains new first-/last-mile options. Apply 6-month slip from original 2027 target already baked into 2028 estimate. Score impact: connectivity S1 uplift for Jurong West and CCK sub-zones currently under-served by rail.

pipeline_items.description: Jurong Region Line (JRL) Stage 2: 7-station eastern branch from Tengah to Pandan Reservoir (JE1–JE7), interchange at Jurong East (EWL/NSL). Opens 2028.
pipeline_items.notes: Tengah new town BTO residents currently have zero MRT access. JRL Stage 2 is Tengah's primary rail provision milestone — transforms it from G-archetype (early-stage, car-dependent) to a provisioned estate. Jurong East gains an additional JRL interchange on top of existing EWL/NSL/CCL. Tengah Plantation and Tengah Park are key stations. Stage 2 nominally co-opens with Stage 1 in 2028 per LTA planning.

pipeline_items.description: Jurong Region Line (JRL) Stage 3: Extension to NTU campus (Peng Kang Hill) and Jurong Pier, adding 7 stations (JS9–JS12, JW3–JW5). Opens 2029.
pipeline_items.notes: Serves NTU corridor and Jurong industrial/pier area. Residential estate uplift modest — mainly NTU vicinity and Jurong Pier industrial zone. Peng Kang Hill station serves western Tengah fringe. Long-dated; treat as PLANNED not GAZETTED. Apply standard time-discount in Provision momentum scoring.

pipeline_items.description: Cross Island Line (CRL) Phase 1: 12-station east-west backbone from Aviation Park (CR2) to Bright Hill (CR13). Interchanges at Pasir Ris (EWL), Hougang (NEL), Ang Mo Kio (NSL), Bright Hill (TEL). Target 2030.
pipeline_items.notes: Construction commenced 2023; LTA target 2030. Pasir Ris gains a second line (currently only EWL) — structurally most impactful for Pasir Ris Value uplift given current under-pricing. Tampines gains Tampines North (CR5) and Aviation Park stops. Hougang gets a direct rail link to the east without changing lines. Ang Mo Kio and Serangoon North benefit from east-west corridor access. Also serves Loyang and Defu industrial areas. >100,000 households in catchment. CRL is the single largest pending Provision uplift in the pipeline — Pasir Ris and Hougang are highest beneficiaries relative to current Provision score.

pipeline_items.description: Kaki Bukit Polyclinic — 18 Jalan Damai, co-located with nursing home and kidney dialysis centre, operated by SingHealth Polyclinics. Near Kaki Bukit MRT. Confirmed address. Construction started H2 2024 after delays; originally targeted 2025, then slipped to 2026, now grouped in the MOH March 2025 press release's 'by 2027' batch. TOP expected 2026 but operational opening likely 2027.
pipeline_items.notes: MOH confirmed site at 18 Jalan Damai. Construction started mid-2024 per parliamentary confirmation. Original target 2025, MOH formally delayed to 2026, then 2025 MOH press release bundles it 'by 2027'. Serves Kaki Bukit and Bedok residents. MOH source: Update on Integrated Development at Jalan Damai (moh.gov.sg).

pipeline_items.description: Yew Tee Polyclinic — 628 Yew Tee Close, NUP's 8th polyclinic, occupying 4 levels (~5,000 sqm) in a 'vertical kampung' mixed development. In Choa Chu Kang planning area near Yew Tee MRT. TOP expected September 2026, operational opening 2027. One of three NUP polyclinics opening in sequence after Tengah (opened Feb 2026).
pipeline_items.notes: Confirmed address 628 Yew Tee Close. NUP confirmed as operator. TOP expected Sep 2026. Yew Tee is in Choa Chu Kang district — not one of our core estates but SEMBAWANG is the nearest estate in our list. Also serves CCK residents who are outside our estate set. MOH 'facilities from 2026 onwards' page lists it.

pipeline_items.description: Bidadari Polyclinic — 51 Alkaff Crescent, Upper Aljunied Road, co-located with nursing home. Operated by NHGP. Approximately 500m from Woodleigh MRT (NEL). Serves Bidadari estate and surrounding District 13 (Alkaff, Woodleigh, Bartley). Part of integrated development with nursing home. On track for 2027 per early-2026 update.
pipeline_items.notes: Confirmed address 51 Alkaff Crescent per MOH 'polyclinic in Bidadari along Upper Aljunied Road' press release and 'facilities from 2026 onwards' page. NHGP operator. Bidadari sits between Serangoon and Toa Payoh towns. Primary beneficiary from our estate list is SERANGOON. Status confirmed 'on track' as of early 2026.

pipeline_items.description: Taman Jurong Polyclinic — 20 Yung Kuang Road (also cited as former West Point Hospital site, 235 Corporation Drive). NUP-operated, elderly-friendly features. Serves Jurong residents alongside Pioneer and Jurong Polyclinics. Dedicated 2022 MOH announcement gave 2028 target; 2025 MOH press release groups it with Bishan as 'by 2030' — treat 2028 as primary target with 2030 as backstop.
pipeline_items.notes: Dual address in sources: '20 Yung Kuang Road' (MOH 2026 facilities page) and '235 Corporation Drive / former West Point Hospital' (MOH 2022 press release). These may refer to the same site or a revised location — verify before scoring. 2022 MOH press release explicitly stated 2028; 2025 MOH press release grouped it as 'by 2030' with Bishan. Use 2028 as primary, apply SlipPremium. NUP operator confirmed.

pipeline_items.description: Bishan Polyclinic — New polyclinic in Bishan planning area. Address TBA as of June 2026. Announced in March 2020 COE/parliamentary response following MP feedback. Scheduled 'by 2030' in all MOH communications from 2020 through March 2025. No confirmed site, no construction start as of June 2026.
pipeline_items.notes: Announced by MOH in March 2020 as part of polyclinic expansion. Consistently listed as 'by 2030' across all MOH press releases. No site confirmed as of June 2026 (MOH 'facilities from 2026 onwards' page shows 'Address TBA'). No construction start confirmed. Apply full SlipPremium — this is the last of the 10 new polyclinics and has the least construction certainty. Bishan currently served by no polyclinic within its planning area (nearest: Toa Payoh and Ang Mo Kio polyclinics).

pipeline_items.description: Toa Payoh Polyclinic redevelopment — Existing Toa Payoh Polyclinic to be rebuilt at a new site between Lorong 6 Toa Payoh and PIE. Larger, more modern facility replacing the current one. Not new provision but materially increases capacity and accessibility for Toa Payoh residents. Part of 6-polyclinic redevelopment programme by 2030.
pipeline_items.notes: Confirmed site location 'between Lorong 6 Toa Payoh and the PIE' per MOH 'facilities from 2026 onwards' page. This is a redevelopment (existing polyclinic rebuilt), not new provision — it does not add a net new polyclinic to the national count. However, it upgrades capacity, accessibility, and services for TOA PAYOH. Should be flagged as a redevelopment when used in scoring: it does not lift the Provision score from 'no polyclinic' to 'has polyclinic' but may lift it from 'dated facility' to 'modern facility' margin.

pipeline_items.description: Queenstown Polyclinic redevelopment — Existing Queenstown Polyclinic to be rebuilt along Tanglin Halt Road. Part of 6-polyclinic redevelopment programme by 2030. Increases capacity and modernity for Queenstown residents.
pipeline_items.notes: Confirmed new site 'along Tanglin Halt Road' per MOH 'facilities from 2026 onwards' page. Same caveat as Toa Payoh: this is a redevelopment, not new-to-area provision. Queenstown already has a polyclinic so the Provision S4 (healthcare) score is not enhanced by presence but by modernity/capacity. Flag accordingly. MOH 2025 press release confirms 'by 2030' target.

pipeline_items.description: Heart of Yew Tee Hawker Centre — CCK's first-ever hawker centre, integrated into the Heart of Yew Tee mixed-use development (10-storey residential + 6-storey commercial block) a short walk from Yew Tee MRT station. Includes community club, polyclinic, kidney dialysis centre, and retail. Announced under HDB Remaking Our Heartland (ROH) programme Oct 2023; reaffirmed in URA Draft Masterplan 2025. NEA-managed. Q1 2027 target.
pipeline_items.notes: Three independent primary sources (HDB press release Oct 2023, URA Masterplan 2025, MSE written PQ reply) all cite Q1 2027. This is CCK town's inaugural NEA hawker centre — the town currently has none. Construction is underway. High confidence on year.

pipeline_items.description: CCK Town Centre Hawker Centre — second new hawker centre for Choa Chu Kang, part of a new mixed-use development at the town centre adjacent to Choa Chu Kang MRT (NSL). Will be integrated with a new Integrated Transport Hub replacing the current bus interchange. Announced under HDB ROH CCK (Oct 2023). Cannot start construction until after JRL Phase 1 completes (~2027), then will take several years.
pipeline_items.notes: MSE written PQ reply explicitly states work commences only after JRL Phase 1 (~2027). Site not yet finalised; agencies 'studying development plans'. Earliest realistic opening 2030–2032. Year 2031 is a midpoint estimate — treat as indicative only.

pipeline_items.description: Chong Pang City Hawker Centre and Market (Yishun) — rebuilt and expanded replacement for the existing Chong Pang Market and Hawker Centre, as part of the 0.9ha Chong Pang City integrated development. Partners: NEA, SLA, PA, SportSG. Topping-out ceremony held April 2026. Existing hawkers offered relocation priority.
pipeline_items.notes: Topping-out ceremony completed April 18 2026 (SLA press release). Official target is 2027. NEA is a named co-developer. This is a replacement/upgrade of an existing facility, not a greenfield centre, but it will be materially larger and improved.

pipeline_items.description: Chencharu Hawker Centre (Yishun North) — new NEA-managed hawker centre in Yishun's Chencharu housing area, co-located with the new Chencharu Bus Interchange (Yishun's 2nd interchange) as part of a mixed-use integrated development. NEA confirmed via press release June 12 2024. HDB land tender awarded September 2025.
pipeline_items.notes: NEA press release June 2024 confirms the hawker centre; HDB tender awarded Sep 2025. Completion ~2029 inferred from HDB document reference to sheltered linkway opening 'by 1Q 2029 or upon completion of Bus Interchange, whichever is earlier' (user-cited HDB doc on LandTransportGuru). No official NEA opening year published. Verify before scoring runs.

pipeline_items.description: Bishan Hawker Centre and Integrated Transport Hub — first-ever hawker centre in Bishan, planned for the 2nd floor of a new Bishan Integrated Transport Hub building near the existing bus interchange and Bishan MRT. Part of the Bishan sub-regional centre redevelopment under URA Draft Masterplan 2025. Minister Chee Hong Tat (June 2025) committed work will start within this term of government. Full 7ha business white development (JTC) expected mid-2030s.
pipeline_items.notes: Ministerial commitment (Straits Times June 27 2025) to start work this term (2025–2030), but construction will take 'several years'. Full complex is mid-2030s; hawker centre on 2F of ITH could open earlier. No gazette, no confirmed site boundary, no tender. Bishan previously had no NEA hawker centre and MSE explicitly declined to build one in an earlier PQ (pre-2025). This reversal is driven by the sub-regional centre upgrade. Treat year as speculative; 2032–2035 range credible.

pipeline_items.description: Five unlocated new hawker centres under Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme 2.0 (HUP 2.0) — Singapore government committed in March 2025 to build five additional hawker centres serving both new and existing estates, on top of Bukit Batok West (opened Jan 2025) and Punggol Coast (opened Jul 2025). Locations not disclosed. MSE said details to be shared 'when ready'.
pipeline_items.notes: NEA/MSE press release March 2025 confirmed quantum (5 centres) but no locations. Cannot assign to specific estates without speculation. Year 2030 is a rough midpoint of the 20–30 year HUP 2.0 programme horizon — purely indicative. Woodlands, Tengah, and other underserved areas are commonly cited as likely candidates but are unconfirmed. Do not score specific estates against these until locations are disclosed.

pipeline_items.description: Tengah Parc Point Neighbourhood Centre — polyclinic (NUP), supermarket, food court, retail and dining opened Q1 2026. Serves as interim civic hub for Park District residents. Not to be confused with the main car-free Tengah Town Centre (linked to Tengah MRT), which opens with JRL Stage 2.
pipeline_items.notes: Parc Point is a neighbourhood centre, not the masterplanned car-free Town Centre. The full Tengah Town Centre with Tengah MRT station is a Stage 2 JRL project targeted mid-2028. Tengah Bus Interchange opened July 2024 but is a temporary facility; permanent interchange will relocate to town centre area near MRT.

pipeline_items.description: Tengah Town Centre (car-free) — Singapore's first car-free town centre, integrated with Tengah MRT station (JRL Stage 2). Will include Tengah Mall, permanent bus interchange, and community facilities in the Park District.
pipeline_items.notes: Tied to Jurong Region Line Stage 2 opening mid-2028. Masterplan confirmed by URA/HDB. Tengah General and Community Hospital planned early 2030s. Full town population target 42,000 homes. Provision scoring should use 2028 horizon for this item.

pipeline_items.description: Jurong Gateway Hub (Jurong Lake District) — Integrated Transport Hub at Jurong East MRT station. Combines bus interchange with offices, shops, library, community club, and sports facilities above. Fifth ITH in the West Region.
pipeline_items.notes: Jurong Region Line station at Jurong East completes 2028; Jurong Gateway Hub completes 2029 per JLD official timeline. Cross Island Line Phase 2 (JLD station CR19) adds further connectivity by 2032. JLD also has new Science Centre 2027, Chinese/Japanese Garden rejuvenation completed 2024. Jurong East benefits most directly; Clementi gains CRL interchange by 2032.

pipeline_items.description: Jurong Lake District — Cross Island Line Phase 2 station (CR19), creating a major interchange node within JLD linking west and central Singapore.
pipeline_items.notes: LTA awarded civil contract for CRL JLD station and tunnels in July 2024. Phase 2 includes Maju, Clementi, West Coast and Jurong Lake District stations. Civil contract award is a strong certainty signal; rail SlipPremium applies (discount promises by 0.85).

pipeline_items.description: Woodlands Gateway — 35ha mixed-use district integrated with RTS Link (Woodlands North station) and Woodlands North MRT. Includes transport hub, flexible industrial/office space, and commercial/lifestyle amenities. JTC masterplanning.
pipeline_items.notes: Phase 1 target ~2030. Subsequent phases progressive. RTS Link (Johor Bahru–Singapore) confirmed operational end-2026, first train demo completed February 2026. Woodlands Checkpoint expansion works commence 2025, fully operational 2032. North-South Corridor opens in phases from 2027. This significantly lifts Woodlands Regional Centre anchor role.

pipeline_items.description: RTS Link (Johor Bahru–Singapore Rapid Transit System) — Woodlands North MRT to Bukit Chagar JB. Operationally imminent, dramatically boosting Woodlands as a cross-border transit node.
pipeline_items.notes: First train demo completed at Woodlands North in February 2026. Fares S$5–7 per journey. Five-minute journey to Bukit Chagar. Operationally targeted end-2026. This is the highest-certainty near-term item for the north region.

pipeline_items.description: Hougang Central Integrated Transport Hub — major mixed-use development above Hougang MRT (NE14), integrating new bus interchange, town plaza, ~300,000 sqft retail (largest mall in Hougang), ~830 residential units. Connects NEL and future CRL.
pipeline_items.notes: GLS site awarded January 14, 2026 to CapitaLand-UOL consortium at S$1.5B (S$1,179 psf ppr). Commercial completion expected 2030/2031. Construction hoarding began Q2 2026. Cross Island Line connection adds further value by 2030. This is a CONFIRMED item with land award executed — high certainty.

pipeline_items.description: Punggol Digital District (PDD) — 50ha tech business park. Phase 1 (21ha) opened progressively from Q3 2024. Anchor tenants include GovTech, CSA, OCBC and UOB (moving by 2027). Punggol Coast MRT opened December 2024, bus interchange June 2025.
pipeline_items.notes: Full 50ha targeting 28,000 digital economy jobs by 2030. LaunchPad @ PDD opens in phases from late 2026. Hotel planned H1 2027. For estate scoring, PDD lifts employment accessibility scores for Punggol and Sengkang significantly. Teck Lee LRT opened August 2024.

pipeline_items.description: Tampines North Integrated Transport Hub — seamlessly integrated with Tampines North Cross Island Line station (future CRL Phase 1). Includes bus interchange, hawker centre, community club, and new amenities.
pipeline_items.notes: Construction commenced 2024. Tied to CRL Tampines North station completion; CRL Phase 1 expected ~2030. One-year delay previously noted due to COVID-19 impact on CRL works. Currently served by Tampines North Bus Interchange as interim. The CRL tie-in means this should use rail SlipPremium (0.85) on timing confidence.

pipeline_items.description: Canberra Plaza — New Generation Neighbourhood Centre (NGNC) directly linked to Canberra MRT station. Three commercial storeys, ~11,000 sqm, with supermarket, food courts, restaurants, medical clinics, water playground, and community plaza.
pipeline_items.notes: Opened 18 December 2020. Fully operational. BCA Green Mark Platinum award. Transit-oriented design with footbridge to Canberra MRT. This is ALREADY OPEN — for pipeline scoring purposes, treat as existing provision, not a future uplift. Relevant for Canberra estate current-state scoring.

pipeline_items.description: Pioneer Primary School relocates from Jurong West to 80 Tengah Garden Avenue — first mainstream school in Tengah new town, admitting P1 from 2026.
pipeline_items.notes: Confirmed by MOE Feb 2023 press release and school profile. School relocated to Tengah Garden Avenue. First of three planned primaries for Tengah.

pipeline_items.description: Outram Secondary School relocates from York Hill to 48 Anchorvale Crescent, Sengkang — first S1 intake at Sengkang campus from 2026. Dual-campus operation until 2027.
pipeline_items.notes: Confirmed MOE Jan 2024 press release. Addresses secondary school demand from Punggol/Sengkang population growth. Not a brand-new school — relocation of existing OSS.

pipeline_items.description: New unnamed secondary school planned for Sengkang to address independent demand from Punggol/Sengkang growth — distinct from Outram Secondary relocation.
pipeline_items.notes: MOE Feb 2023 press release stated new secondary school in Sengkang 'beginning operations in 2026'. Opening year flagged as tentative by MOE. School name not yet announced.

pipeline_items.description: Kranji Primary School and MK@Kranji relocate from Choa Chu Kang to a new Tengah campus — second primary school in Tengah.
pipeline_items.notes: MOE Jan 2024 press release. School stopped accepting P1/K1 from 2025. Opening year flagged tentative by MOE. Not a new school — relocation.

pipeline_items.description: Anglo-Chinese School (Primary) relocates from Barker Road to Tengah and becomes co-educational — third primary school in Tengah.
pipeline_items.notes: MOE Feb 2023 press release. ACS(J) at Winstedt Road consolidating. Co-educational from 2030. Opening year flagged tentative by MOE. Significant name-brand school adding to Tengah provision.

pipeline_items.description: Townsville Primary School relocates from Ang Mo Kio to East Canberra (Sembawang) — first mainstream primary in Canberra East precinct.
pipeline_items.notes: MOE May 2025 press release. School stops P1 intake 2025–2027. Current campus operates through 2030 for existing cohorts. Addresses Canberra BTO demand.

pipeline_items.description: Damai Primary School relocates from Bedok to Tampines Street 64 — new campus serves Tampines North BTO residents.
pipeline_items.notes: MOE May 2025 press release / Damai Primary official announcement. MK@Damai co-located. Dual-campus 2029–2030. Tampines North, not Tampines central.

pipeline_items.description: New unnamed primary school planned for Tampines North with co-located MOE Kindergarten.
pipeline_items.notes: MOE Jan 2024 press release. School name and exact address not yet announced. Separate from Damai Primary relocation.

pipeline_items.description: Two new primary schools planned for Chencharu/Yishun North and Woodlands North Coast (North Coast estate) by 2031.
pipeline_items.notes: MOE May 2025 press release. Named as serving 'Chencharu, Yishun' and 'North Coast, Woodlands' new estates. Names not yet announced. Both targeted by 2031.

pipeline_items.description: Catholic Junior College relocates from Whitley Road to Punggol, in the vicinity of Punggol Digital District — first JC in north-east Singapore.
pipeline_items.notes: Announced by MOE 16 Jan 2026 under Junior College Rejuvenation Programme. Campus targeted tentatively 2034. Significantly reduces travel time for JC-bound students in north-east. No new JC built — relocation of CJC.

pipeline_items.description: Pathlight School 3 permanent campus near Punggol Digital District — serves students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD-NC).
pipeline_items.notes: MOE Feb 2023 press release. Tentative opening 2032. Relocated from former Chong Boon Primary/Secondary site. Third Pathlight campus nationally.

pipeline_items.description: Woodlands Health Campus (now renamed Woodlands Hospital as of Jan 2026) — 680 beds operational, ramping to 1,800 beds total. Serves north and north-west.
pipeline_items.notes: Opened 13 July 2024. Renamed Woodlands Hospital 2 Jan 2026. Currently 680 acute + community beds. Ramp-up to 1,800 beds targeted by 2030 (+400 beds per MOH plan). NUHS-operated.

pipeline_items.description: Eastern General Hospital Campus at Bedok North — integrated general hospital (~1,000 beds) and community hospital (~400 beds), opening progressively from 2029.
pipeline_items.notes: SingHealth-operated. Piling completed; main construction commenced Aug 2025 (Obayashi-Santarli JV). ~250,000 sqm nine-storey campus. Virtual services already operational. Planned progressive opening 2029 — no confirmed single opening date.

pipeline_items.description: St Andrew's Community Hospital new facility in Bedok — 240 beds (140 Transitional Care Facility beds) opened 2025.
pipeline_items.notes: Already operational as of 2025. Rehabilitative and transitional care. Partially reduces gap ahead of Eastern General Hospital opening.

pipeline_items.description: Alexandra Hospital redevelopment — ageing 326-bed facility rebuilt into integrated general hospital with ~1,300 beds plus ~400-bed nursing home, opening progressively from 2028.
pipeline_items.notes: Groundbreaking May 2024. Construction commenced 2025. Decade-long project. Two new buildings. Transforms southern Singapore hospital provision.

pipeline_items.description: Tengah General and Community Hospital — new integrated hospital for western Singapore operated by NUHS, complementing NTFGH and Jurong Community Hospital.
pipeline_items.notes: Announced March 2024 by MOH / Health Minister Ong Ye Kung. Official timeline is 'early 2030s' — no specific year confirmed. NUHS cluster. No groundbreaking date announced yet. Treats as ~2032 placeholder.

pipeline_items.description: Tan Tock Seng Hospital Medical Tower at HealthCity Novena — ~600 new acute beds and expanded emergency department as part of HealthCity Novena Master Plan.
pipeline_items.notes: Project launched Sep 2025. Exact opening year not confirmed — estimated mid-2030s per HealthCity Novena plan. NHG-operated. Second phase of HealthCity Novena redevelopment. Placeholder year used.

pipeline_items.description: NUH Kent Ridge Campus redevelopment Phase 1 — replaces half of existing 1,200 beds and adds ~100 net new beds, targeting 2033.
pipeline_items.notes: MOH confirmed phased redevelopment. Phase 2 by 2038 adds another 200 beds to reach 1,500 total. No groundbreaking announced yet. Not an expansion of net capacity in early phase.

pipeline_items.description: Bidadari Polyclinic co-located with Orange Valley Nursing Home at 51 Alkaff Crescent, Upper Aljunied Road, near Woodleigh MRT (~500m).
pipeline_items.notes: MOH confirmed location (Upper Aljunied Road near Woodleigh station). Part of five polyclinics targeted by 2027. Co-located nursing home adds elderly care capacity to Bidadari estate.

pipeline_items.description: Tengah Polyclinic — new polyclinic serving the Tengah new town.
pipeline_items.notes: MOH confirmed as one of five polyclinics by 2027. Exact address not yet published. Critical gap-filler for Tengah which currently has zero healthcare infrastructure.

pipeline_items.description: Yew Tee Polyclinic at 628 Yew Tee Close — new polyclinic serving Yew Tee and Choa Chu Kang north.
pipeline_items.notes: MOH confirmed address (628 Yew Tee Close). Part of five polyclinics by 2027. Reduces load on Choa Chu Kang Polyclinic.

pipeline_items.description: Kaki Bukit Polyclinic co-located with Lentor Health Nursing Home at 18 Jalan Damai — new polyclinic in Kaki Bukit / Bedok North fringe.
pipeline_items.notes: MOH confirmed address. Co-located nursing home. Part of five polyclinics by 2027. Bridges coverage between Bedok Polyclinic and Eastern General Hospital (opening 2029).

pipeline_items.description: Serangoon Polyclinic at junction of Upper Serangoon Road and Serangoon Central — new polyclinic for Serangoon estate.
pipeline_items.notes: MOH confirmed location. Originally announced to open 2025, delayed to 2027. Part of five polyclinics by 2027 MOH target.

pipeline_items.description: Bishan Polyclinic — new polyclinic serving Bishan estate, currently underserved relative to population density.
pipeline_items.notes: MOH listed as upcoming facility (facilities-from-2026 page). Address TBA. Part of expansion from 26 to 32 polyclinics by 2030. No confirmed opening date beyond 'by 2030'.

pipeline_items.description: Taman Jurong Polyclinic at 20 Yung Kuang Road — new polyclinic serving Taman Jurong estate and Jurong West.
pipeline_items.notes: MOH confirmed address (20 Yung Kuang Road). MOH Clementi Polyclinic Jun 2022 press release placed this at 2028; current MOH facility list categorises as post-2026. Cross-check: use 2028–2030 range.

pipeline_items.description: Rail Corridor (South) Phase 2 trail improvement works — Henderson Road to Spooner Road section under heavy reconstruction with stronger foundation. Phase 1 (Jalan Kilang Barat to Henderson Road) reopened 2 March 2026 ahead of schedule. Phase 2 closure runs March 2026 to July 2027. Full south section (Tanjong Pagar–Queenstown–Buona Vista corridor) will be continuous trail once complete.
pipeline_items.notes: NParks FAQ and closure notices confirm Phase 2 completion target 31 July 2027. Development of former Tanjong Pagar Railway Station begins only after 2028 (post-Cantonment MRT Circle Line 6 completion). Sources: railcorridor.nparks.gov.sg/faq/, Wikipedia Rail Corridor (Singapore).

pipeline_items.description: Rail Corridor — Jurong Branch Line PCN: New trail following the path of the former Jurong railway line branching off near Bukit Timah, cutting through Clementi Forest and towards Jurong/Pasir Panjang. Construction started early 2025, opening progressively from end-2026. Connects Bukit Timah node to western industrial belt via Clementi Forest and Dover Forest fringe.
pipeline_items.notes: Wikipedia Rail Corridor (Singapore) and PCN cycling changelog both confirm construction started early 2025, progressive opening from end-2026. Route passes through Clementi Forest (near Dover/Clementi estates). Not to be confused with the Jurong Region Line MRT. Branch follows the historical 19km Jurong industrial railway alignment.

pipeline_items.description: Rail Corridor — Queensway Community Node: New community and recreational node at Queensway along the Rail Corridor, serving the Queenstown estate. Design competition held September 2024. Adds active recreation and heritage interpretation functions at the Queensway junction of the corridor.
pipeline_items.notes: URA Draft Master Plan Rail Corridor page confirms Queensway Node completion targeted by 2027. One of six additional community nodes planned along the 24km corridor beyond the four already implemented.

pipeline_items.description: Rail Corridor — Stagmont Ring Community Node: Planned community node at the northern end of the Rail Corridor near Bukit Panjang/Choa Chu Kang area. Long-lead-time node at the northern corridor.
pipeline_items.notes: URA Master Plan and Wikipedia cite 2035 target for Stagmont Ring. Rail Garden @ CCK (Choa Chu Kang) targeted 2028. Bukit Batok benefits from proximity to CCK node.

pipeline_items.description: Tengah Forest Corridor: 5km linear green corridor running through the heart of Tengah eco-town, connecting the new town to the Central and Western Catchment Nature Reserves. 40-metre wide spine with paved paths for pedestrians and cyclists. Wildlife passage designed for safe animal movement. Part of HDB's Forest Town masterplan with Bukit Batok Nature Corridor linking to it.
pipeline_items.notes: Confirmed by HDB Tengah masterplan and NParks. No firm standalone opening date published — phased with BTO completions (Parc Flora Q3 2025, Plantation Creek Q2 2026, Parc Meadow June 2027). Bukit Batok Nature Corridor (separate item) starts construction 2026 and connects to this corridor from 2028. Estimate 2028 for meaningful public access as Tengah population builds up.

pipeline_items.description: Tengah Central Park: 20-hectare central park in Tengah town centre, car-free precinct with amphitheatre, natural water features, waterfront promenade, and community spaces. Core green anchor for the Park District of Tengah.
pipeline_items.notes: Confirmed in HDB Tengah masterplan. No NParks-issued standalone opening date. Likely phases with early BTO completions. Jurong Region Line Tengah stations (3 stops) slated for mid-2028 which will drive footfall. Treat as PLANNED — subject to BTO and JRL schedule slippage.

pipeline_items.description: Bulim Park (Jurong West/Tengah border): 14-football-field park at Bulim Avenue adjacent to Jurong Innovation District. West section (2.13ha) opened December 2025/January 2026. Full park includes 3-storey sheltered net playground, nature playgarden, rain garden, and connection to 11km Sky Corridor elevated walking/cycling path over Jurong Innovation District.
pipeline_items.notes: West section confirmed open January 2026 per NParks park detail page and multiple media reports. Full Sky Corridor (11km) completion timeline not confirmed — treat full park connectivity as PLANNED. Nearest MRT: Boon Lay. Primarily serves Jurong West and will serve Tengah once JRL opens.

pipeline_items.description: Punggol Heritage Trail: 1.3km linear park following the historical Old Punggol Road alignment, connecting Punggol Waterway Park to Punggol Point Park. First 400m (from Punggol North Avenue to Campus Boulevard) opened 23 August 2025. Adventure Playground and Backwoods Trail expected end-2025. Remaining 900m with conserved Api Api Ludat mangrove trees and connection to Punggol Jetty completing early 2027.
pipeline_items.notes: NParks press release (August 2025) confirms first stretch open and full completion timeline. Integrates with SIT campus, Punggol Digital District, Punggol Waterway, and the 26km North-Eastern Riverine Loop PCN. Remaining 900m originally stated end-2026 but SmartLocal article cites early 2027.

pipeline_items.description: Jurong Lake Gardens — fully completed with opening of rejuvenated Chinese and Japanese Gardens on 8 September 2024. The 90-hectare national gardens in the heartlands now comprises all three sections: Lakeside Garden (completed April 2023), and the reopened Chinese and Japanese Gardens featuring Singapore's largest water lily collection, new floral gardens, visitor pavilions, and lakeside recreational spaces.
pipeline_items.notes: Already delivered as of 2024. No further extensions announced. Fully completed — no pipeline risk. Listed here for completeness as a major recently-delivered green asset. Benefits estates within cycling/walking distance: Jurong East, Jurong West, and to a lesser extent Clementi.

pipeline_items.description: Round Island Route PCN — Western Half (Phase 2): Completing the remaining ~75km of the 150km Round Island Route around Singapore's western and northern coastlines. Phase 1 (75km eastern half from Rower's Bay NE to Berlayer Creek south) launched January 2022 and is fully open. Western half under progressive construction targeting 2035 completion to create a true 150km loop.
pipeline_items.notes: NParks press release on Phase 1 completion and pcn.nparks.gov.sg/know-our-pcn/rir/ confirm 2035 target for full 150km route. Western section passes through northern coast (Woodlands, Sembawang, Canberra) and southern coast. No intermediate milestones publicly announced. High slip risk given 9-year horizon.

pipeline_items.description: Bukit Batok Nature Corridor revamp: 10km of trails connecting Bukit Timah Nature Reserve to the upcoming Tengah Forest Corridor. New boardwalk, observation decks overlooking a quarry, play areas, exercise plazas, and additional arrival nodes. Construction starts 2026, opening in stages from 2028.
pipeline_items.notes: Announced January 2025 per Timeout Singapore report citing NParks. Construction start 2026 confirmed. Stages from 2028. Physically bridges Bukit Timah Nature Reserve and Tengah Forest Corridor — critical ecological link for Bukit Batok residents. Source: timeout.com Mandai/Bukit Batok NParks announcement Jan 2025.

pipeline_items.description: Mandai Mangrove and Mudflat Nature Park: New 72.8-hectare nature park in Mandai, featuring over 380 wildlife species, two observation nodes with panoramic mudflat views, coastal trails, wooden bird hides, and ecological connection to Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve. Construction starts 2026, open from 2028.
pipeline_items.notes: NParks announcement January 2025 (Timeout Singapore). Construction starts 2026. Benefits Woodlands and Sembawang residents as nearest major estates. Adds significant nature-access uplift to Woodlands, which currently lacks major nature parks (Woodlands Waterfront Park is the main existing asset). Kranji Nature Corridor links this to Central Catchment — more than 11km of Nature Ways connecting along Woodlands Road and Kranji Loop.

pipeline_items.description: WoodsVista Gallery — 1.9km elevated walking and cycling path in Woodlands North Coast, developed by HDB and NParks. Phase 1 constructed alongside UrbanVille @ Woodlands BTO (targeted completion 2026), connecting Woodlands North Coast district to Woodlands Central and Woodlands MRT station. Ties into the Round Island Route and Rail Corridor network.
pipeline_items.notes: Referenced in HDB Woodlands North Coast development plans. Phase 1 tied to UrbanVille @ Woodlands BTO expected completion 2026. Described as a walking and cycling gallery — similar in concept to Bishan-Thomson park connectors. No NParks standalone press release found; treat as PLANNED pending formal gazette.

pipeline_items.description: Tengah PCN cycling path network expansion: ~5.5km of new cycling paths added across Tengah in 2025 along Tengah Road, Tengah Drive, Tengah Boulevard, Plantation Crescent, Garden Avenue, and related streets. Builds out the intra-town cycling spine ahead of Jurong Region Line opening.
pipeline_items.notes: PCN cycling paths changelog documents additions across February, August, and November 2025. Approximately 5.5km net new paths within Tengah town. Already built — operational. Significance is MEDIUM as it is incremental path provision, not a new park or major corridor.

pipeline_items.description: Woodlands Marsiling SERS (announced 26 May 2022): Blocks 212–218 Marsiling Crescent/Lane (732 sold flats, 53 rental flats) acquired to make way for Woodlands Checkpoint expansion. Replacement site: ~1,100 new flats at Woodlands Street 13 (Marsiling Ridge BTO, 292 units; Marsiling Grove BTO also part of replacement pipeline). Replacement flat construction commenced Q3 2023, completion Q4 2027. Residents required to vacate by Q2 2028. Woodlands Checkpoint civil works start Q3 2025, 10–15 year build-out. This is the last confirmed SERS project in Singapore — HDB confirmed on 10 Aug 2025 no further SERS sites are planned.
pipeline_items.notes: Replacement flats complete Q4 2027. Residents move out Q2 2028. Net effect on Woodlands provision: +1,100 new flats on fresh 99-yr leases, loss of 9 old blocks. Checkpoint redevelopment is infrastructure, not provision. Score impact: minimal direct provision change for Woodlands estate — momentum signal only. This is the last SERS exercise under the current policy.

pipeline_items.description: HDB confirmed on 10 August 2025 (National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat) that there are NO further SERS projects planned. All potential high-redevelopment-value sites have already been selected. No new SERS announced for Queenstown, Bukit Merah, Clementi, Kallang/Whampoa, or Bedok in 2025–2026.
pipeline_items.notes: Negative finding — confirmed absence of SERS pipeline for all queried estates. Any SERS speculation for these areas should be marked as RUMOUR or excluded from scoring. VERS (see next item) replaces SERS as the policy mechanism.

pipeline_items.description: HDB VERS (Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme): Government confirmed focus is on developing VERS framework, targeting rollout to a few pilot sites in the first half of the 2030s. Expands to more estates by late 2030s. Key details (voting threshold, compensation formula, replacement flat lease options) not yet announced. Likely target estates include mature towns with 1970s-built flats: Queenstown, Bukit Merah, Toa Payoh, Ang Mo Kio, Bedok, Tampines, Yishun. No estates officially selected as of June 2026.
pipeline_items.notes: VERS is voluntary (residents vote), so redevelopment is not guaranteed. Unlike SERS, VERS does not necessarily produce a windfall or fresh-lease replacement flat — framework details TBD. Score impact is speculative until framework is finalised. Do not model as provision uplift — treat as long-horizon tail risk for lease decay mitigation only.

pipeline_items.description: Tengah Polyclinic opened 28 February 2026 at Parc Point Neighbourhood Centre (Park District). It is Singapore's 28th polyclinic and NUP's first co-located within a neighbourhood centre. Services: chronic disease management, child developmental assessment, immunisation, diagnostics, pharmacy, allied health (physio, psychology, dietetics, podiatry), and Healthier SG enrolment. Parc Point NC (Tengah's 2nd NC after Plantation Plaza) opened Q1 2026 with FairPrice supermarket, Gourmet Paradise foodcourt (14 stalls), Courts, Mr DIY, plus a 190m sheltered retail street.
pipeline_items.notes: Directly scores into Tengah's healthcare (S5) and amenities (S2) provision components. Polyclinic is operational as of 28 Feb 2026 — no discount needed. Parc Point NC also adds meaningful amenity score. Combined with Plantation Plaza (opened June 2024), Tengah now has 2 operational neighbourhood centres. Over 14,000 flats completed (~47% of planned 30,000 units).

pipeline_items.description: Tengah town fill-in BTO progress: 14,000+ flats completed across 14 projects (Park, Plantation, Garden districts leading). Brickland Weave and Forest Hill districts have launches completing 2027–2028. Remaining ~16,000 flats to be delivered progressively. Tengah Town Centre and Central Park civic space planned 'in coming years' — no fixed date published. Pioneer Primary School (Plantation District) opened Q1 2026.
pipeline_items.notes: Town centre completion is ungazetted — treat as PLANNED. ~47% complete on housing stock. Full provision scoring should hold Tengah's density (S4) and momentum (S7) values as improving trajectory, but amenity/commercial scores are still below a mature HDB town. Tengah remains Archetype G (early-stage new town).

pipeline_items.description: Jurong Region Line (JRL) serving Tengah: Phase 1 (West Branch including Tengah station) delayed to mid-2028; Phase 2 (East Branch: Tengah Plantation, Tengah Park stations) also 2028. Original 2026–2027 timeline slipped ~12 months due to COVID construction recovery. Phase 3 (remaining stations) 2029. Full JRL operational mid-2028 to 2029.
pipeline_items.notes: LTA confirmed mid-2028 for Phase 1, 2028 for Phase 2. SlipPremium applies (rail = 0.85). Tengah connectivity (S1) currently near-zero on MRT — JRL opening is the single largest pending provision uplift for this estate. Until keys turn in mid-2028, apply full time-discount. Tengah's S1 score should reflect ~0.85 × 0.5 year discount on JRL contribution.

pipeline_items.description: Brickland MRT Station (NS3A) on North-South Line: new infill station between Bukit Gombak and Choa Chu Kang. LTA awarded S$281M civil contract to Obayashi Corporation; construction begins H1 2026. Passenger service targeted 2034. Will serve Tengah Brickland District, Keat Hong estate, Bukit Batok West, ITE College West, Swiss Cottage Secondary.
pipeline_items.notes: Construction gazetted, but 2034 opening is 8 years out. Apply maximum time discount (Certainty=CONFIRMED × Time=0.5 × SlipPremium=0.85). Primarily benefits Brickland District of Tengah — not yet populated. Augments JRL connectivity; secondary infill rather than primary access. Do not score into current provision runs.

pipeline_items.description: Circle Line Stage 6 (CCL6) opens 12 July 2026: three new stations — Keppel, Cantonment, Prince Edward Road — complete the Circle Line loop connecting HarbourFront to Marina Bay. Public preview 4 July 2026. This directly enhances Bukit Merah connectivity: Bukit Merah residents can reach the waterfront and southern CBD corridor via CCL without interchange.
pipeline_items.notes: LTA confirmed 4 July 2026 public preview, 12 July 2026 full service. No discount needed — effectively operational. Scores into Bukit Merah S1 (Connectivity). Bukit Merah already has EWL (Queenstown, Redhill, Tiong Bahru) and NEL (Havelock). CCL6 adds a southern waterfront axis. Moderate uplift — not a primary station but improves network coverage score.

pipeline_items.description: Remaking Our Heartland Batch 4 (ROH4) — Bukit Merah: Bukit Merah Central, Alexandra Village, and Bukit Purmei town centre upgrades (streetscapes, infrastructure refresh). Enhanced PCN connectivity to Rail Corridor and Southern Ridges. Senior-friendly amenities: barrier-free ramps, exercise trails, social nodes. Alexandra Village NC upgrade with refreshed paving, pocket parks, barrier-free access. ROH4 announced September 2023; works rolling out 2025–2028.
pipeline_items.notes: No single completion date published — phased delivery. ROH upgrades improve S3 (Green/Liveability feel) and marginally S2 (Amenities) and S8 (Infrastructure). Not a step-change provision uplift but materially improves walkability and senior-suitability scores. Useful for Liveability matrix (Retiree/Senior persona) more than raw Provision score.

pipeline_items.description: Remaking Our Heartland Batch 4 (ROH4) — Queenstown: Active Health Fitness Trail in Mei Ling precinct completed by end-2025. Social nodes, cycling infrastructure, garden spaces from 2026 onward. Neighbourhood centre upgrades at Holland Drive, Commonwealth Crescent, Mei Ling Heights, Dawson Place, Farrer Road. New senior-friendly pedestrian infrastructure across precincts.
pipeline_items.notes: Fitness trail (Mei Ling) confirmed complete by end-2025. Social nodes and NC upgrades rolling from 2026. These are incremental enhancements — not new civic builds. Queenstown already scores high on Provision (B+ band). ROH uplift is at the margin: S3 (Green/PCN) and walkability. More significant for Liveability matrix persona fit (Retiree, Young Professional) than raw Provision band change.

pipeline_items.description: Sembawang North BTO and Canberra estate fill-in: June 2026 BTO launch adds ~2,000 flats across two projects on Sembawang Drive and Sungei Sembawang (part of the 53-hectare Sembawang North masterplan for ~10,000 units total: 8,000 BTO + 2,000 private). February 2026 BTO (Sembawang Deck, 777 units) also launched. Civic facilities (childcare centres, bus services) delivered 6 months post-first key collection. Bukit Canberra (polyclinic opened Nov 2023, hawker centre, sports hub) already operational.
pipeline_items.notes: Sembawang North is a long-horizon development (10,000 units over ~15 years). Bukit Canberra polyclinic and hawker centre already built — score these as CONFIRMED. New BTO fill-in raises population density (S4) progressively. Canberra MRT (NSL, opened 2019) is operational. Sembawang Shipyard redevelopment (post-2028) is a longer-term momentum signal. Canberra currently Archetype G transitioning toward F/B depending on completion pace.

pipeline_items.description: NRP 16th Batch (April 2025): 17 HDB neighbourhoods selected including blocks in Bukit Panjang, Sembawang, and Sengkang. Budget raised from S$6,100 to S$6,600 per flat. First batch to include blocks built 1996–1999. Total cost exceeding S$165M, benefiting over 25,000 households. Improvements: residents' corners, seating, covered linkways, drop-off porches, playgrounds, landscaping, senior-friendly amenities. Bedok Reservoir View (Block 775A) and Bedok North Avenue 2 (Block 140) confirmed in this batch.
pipeline_items.notes: NRP funds external block upgrades only — not interior works. Impact on Provision score is marginal (slight S8 infrastructure and S3 amenity feel improvement). Not a material provision uplift for Bedok. Useful as evidence Bedok blocks are receiving baseline maintenance investment, countering lease-decay momentum drag.

pipeline_items.description: Woodlands Health Campus (now Woodlands Hospital): Integrated acute and community hospital serving northern Singapore. Opened July 13, 2024, with official ceremony. Renamed to Woodlands Hospital on January 2, 2026. Comprises 1,000-bed acute hospital, Medical Centre with specialist clinics, and Long Term Care Tower (~400 beds). Fully operational as of June 2026.
pipeline_items.notes: Already open and operational. Renamed from 'Woodlands Health Campus' to 'Woodlands Hospital' on 2 Jan 2026. Primary source: wh.com.sg official opening announcement and PMO speech by SM Lee Hsien Loong.

pipeline_items.description: JB–Singapore RTS Link: 4 km light rail shuttle between Woodlands North MRT station (TEL) and Bukit Chagar station in Johor Bahru. Peak capacity 10,000 pax/hour/direction; ~5 minute journey. Integrated with new CIQ facilities at Woodlands North. First train demo run completed at Woodlands North on February 4, 2026. Targeted passenger service: end-2026.
pipeline_items.notes: LTA official target is end-2026. Construction and systems installation on track as of Feb 2026 per Malaysian Transport Minister. Some reports flag potential slip to early 2027 (unconfirmed). Rail SlipPremium applies per framework rules. Standalone LRT shuttle — NOT a TEL extension. Source: LTA factsheet Jan 2024, Mothership Feb 2026.

pipeline_items.description: Woodlands Checkpoint redevelopment Phase 1: ICA expanding the checkpoint to ~5x current size (19 ha → 95 ha). Phase 1 construction commenced Q3 2025 with new automated clearance lanes for cargo vehicles, arriving cars, and motorcycles. Old Woodlands Town Centre integrated into redevelopment. Progressive completion from 2028; full operations by 2032.
pipeline_items.notes: Construction physically commenced Q3 2025 per ICA press release. Full completion 2032. Significance is medium for residential provision — improves cross-border mobility but not a direct residential amenity. Source: ICA media release.

pipeline_items.description: Woodlands Regional Centre / Woodlands Gateway: ~100 ha mixed commercial-office-industrial precinct across Woodlands Central and Woodlands North Coast. URA North Coast Innovation Corridor anchor. Woodlands Gateway Phase 1 (~35 ha of flexible industrial/office space managed by JTC) expected to complete around 2030. No specific major employer or anchor tenant confirmed as of June 2026. Long-term vision: ~100,000 jobs and 700,000 sqm commercial GFA over 10–15 years.
pipeline_items.notes: No named employer or tenant confirmed for 2025–26 period. JTC Woodlands Gateway Phase 1 ~2030. URA Master Plan 2025 vision only — no gazetted milestones for specific employers. Provision S7 (momentum) input only; cannot flow into measured components. Source: JTC website, URA draft Master Plan 2025.

pipeline_items.description: Canberra Plaza: Neighbourhood mall at Sembawang Crescent/Canberra Link, serving the Canberra/Sembawang North area. Opened December 18, 2020. Anchored by NTUC FairPrice (occupying ~40% GLA), DAISO, A&W, McDonald's, and 30+ lifestyle and dining outlets.
pipeline_items.notes: Already operational since Dec 2020. Not a future development — included as a CONFIRMED provision item for scoring. Source: Wikipedia Canberra Plaza, thesingaporeblog.com.

pipeline_items.description: Sembawang Polyclinic at Bukit Canberra: NHG polyclinic opened November 25, 2023 within the Bukit Canberra Integrated Hub. Co-located with hawker centre (800-seat, 44 stalls), indoor sports hall, ActiveSG gym, swimming pool, senior care centre, and childcare centre. This is the polyclinic serving the Canberra precinct — there is no separate 'Canberra Polyclinic' planned.

The polyclinic is branded 'Sembawang Polyclinic' but physically located at Bukit Canberra within the Canberra-area cluster. No additional Canberra-specific polyclinic is planned or announced beyond this. Source: NHG Health press release, MOH speech.

pipeline_items.description: Bukit Canberra Integrated Hub hawker centre: 800-seat hawker centre with 44 stalls, co-located with the polyclinic, sports hall, and community facilities at Bukit Canberra. Opened alongside the polyclinic complex.

pipeline_items.description: Sembawang North BTO pipeline (Canberra/Sembawang North new town): ~10,000 total homes planned across 53 ha — ~8,000 BTO flats and ~2,000 private units. No dedicated school or community club has been announced for Sembawang North specifically beyond what exists at Bukit Canberra. Source: HDB press releases, uchify.com, 99.co.

pipeline_items.description: Lentor Modern mixed-use development: 90,000 sqft lifestyle mall integrated with Lentor MRT station (TEL). Officially opened January 6, 2026. Anchor tenants: CS Fresh supermarket (12,000 sqft), Mulberry Learning pre-school/childcare (10,000 sqft). 40+ curated tenants including Tim Hortons, Anytime Fitness, Guardian, multiple F&B outlets, music and tuition schools. Three 25-storey residential towers (605 units) above the commercial podium.
pipeline_items.notes: Mall opened 6 Jan 2026 per GuocoLand press release. Supermarket anchor is CS Fresh (Cold Storage upscale brand), NOT NTUC FairPrice. Childcare is Mulberry Learning, not a government-run ECDA centre. Direct basement connection to Lentor MRT. Source: GuocoLand press release Jan 2026, EdgeProp, Alvinology.

top_items.description: Woodlands Marsiling SERS (announced 26 May 2022): Blocks 212–218 Marsiling Crescent/Lane (732 sold flats, 53 rental flats) acquired to make way for Woodlands Checkpoint expansion. Replacement site: ~1,100 new flats at Woodlands Street 13 (Marsiling Ridge BTO, 292 units; Marsiling Grove BTO also part of replacement pipeline). Replacement flat construction commenced Q3 2023, completion Q4 2027. Residents required to vacate by Q2 2028. Woodlands Checkpoint civil works start Q3 2025, 10–15 year build-out. This is the last confirmed SERS project in Singapore — HDB confirmed on 10 Aug 2025 no further SERS sites are planned.

Woodlands Gateway — 35ha mixed-use district integrated with RTS Link (Woodlands North station) and Woodlands North MRT. Includes transport hub, flexible industrial/office space, and commercial/lifestyle amenities. JTC masterplanning.

Woodlands Checkpoint redevelopment Phase 1: ICA expanding the checkpoint to ~5x current size (19 ha → 95 ha). Phase 1 construction commenced Q3 2025 with new automated clearance lanes for cargo vehicles, arriving cars, and motorcycles. Old Woodlands Town Centre integrated into redevelopment. Progressive completion from 2028; full operations by 2032.

Mandai Mangrove and Mudflat Nature Park: New 72.8-hectare nature park in Mandai, featuring over 380 wildlife species, two observation nodes with panoramic mudflat views, coastal trails, wooden bird hides, and ecological connection to Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve. Construction starts 2026, open from 2028.

Woodlands Regional Centre / Woodlands Gateway: ~100 ha mixed commercial-office-industrial precinct across Woodlands Central and Woodlands North Coast. URA North Coast Innovation Corridor anchor. Woodlands Gateway Phase 1 (~35 ha of flexible industrial/office space managed by JTC) expected to complete around 2030. No specific major employer or anchor tenant confirmed as of June 2026. Long-term vision: ~100,000 jobs and 700,000 sqm commercial GFA over 10–15 years.
CRL Phase 1 — CR5 Pasir Ris station (EWL interchange). Serves central Pasir Ris town, connecting CRL to the East-West Line. Opens as part of 12-station Phase 1 bloc.
CRL Phase 1 — CR4 Pasir Ris East station. Serves eastern Pasir Ris residential area along Pasir Ris Drive 1, between Pasir Ris Street 11 and 12.

Cross Island Line (CRL) Phase 1: 12-station east-west backbone from Aviation Park (CR2) to Bright Hill (CR13). Interchanges at Pasir Ris (EWL), Hougang (NEL), Ang Mo Kio (NSL), Bright Hill (TEL). Target 2030.
CRL Punggol Extension — CP1/CR5 Pasir Ris junction station. Acts as the branch node connecting CRL main line to the Punggol Extension spur toward Punggol.
CRL Punggol Extension — CP2 Elias station. New station serving the Elias Road corridor in Pasir Ris / Punggol borderland, providing first rail access to that area.

Taman Jurong Polyclinic — 20 Yung Kuang Road (also cited as former West Point Hospital site, 235 Corporation Drive). NUP-operated, elderly-friendly features. Serves Jurong residents alongside Pioneer and Jurong Polyclinics. Dedicated 2022 MOH announcement gave 2028 target; 2025 MOH press release groups it with Bishan as 'by 2030' — treat 2028 as primary target with 2030 as backstop.

Jurong Gateway Hub (Jurong Lake District) — Integrated Transport Hub at Jurong East MRT station. Combines bus interchange with offices, shops, library, community club, and sports facilities above. Fifth ITH in the West Region.

JRL Stage 2 (JRL East): 7 stations from Tengah Plantation (JE1) to Pandan Reservoir (JE7). Key interchange at Jurong East (JE5/NS1/EW24). Serves the eastern fringe of Tengah new town (Tengah Plantation, Tengah Park), Bukit Batok West (JE3), Toh Guan, and Jurong East. Stage 2 date has not been formally revised since March 2026 — carries the original planned year of 2028.
Jurong Region Line (JRL) Stage 2: 7-station eastern branch from Tengah to Pandan Reservoir (JE1–JE7), interchange at Jurong East (EWL/NSL). Opens 2028.

Jurong Region Line (JRL) serving Tengah: Phase 1 (West Branch including Tengah station) delayed to mid-2028; Phase 2 (East Branch: Tengah Plantation, Tengah Park stations) also 2028. Original 2026–2027 timeline slipped ~12 months due to COVID construction recovery. Phase 3 (remaining stations) 2029. Full JRL operational mid-2028 to 2029.
